content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Translation for Non-Technical Stakeholders"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Bridging the gap between engineering teams and non-technical stakeholders is one of the most critical challenges in software development. Technical translation is the art and science of converting complex architectural concepts, technical debt, and system limitations into clear business value."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Principles of Technical Translation"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Focus on outcomes rather than implementation details."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use analogies that relate to everyday business operations."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Quantify risk and reward in financial or operational terms."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Translating Technical Debt: An Example"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Engineers often struggle to explain why refactoring code is necessary. Instead of saying we need to rewrite legacy microservices using a new framework, frame it as maintenance and risk reduction."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"Technical: \"We must refactor the legacy ORM queries to prevent N+1 select bottlenecks.\"\n\nTranslated: \"We need to optimize our database reporting to cut cloud infrastructure costs and prevent slow load times during peak traffic hours.\""},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Clear Communication"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid jargon unless explicitly defined during the conversation."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prepare visual aids such as flowcharts or high-level architecture diagrams."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always invite questions and verify understanding by asking stakeholders to summarize in their own words."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering technical translation empowers product managers, executives, and clients to make informed decisions without needing a computer science degree. By focusing on impact, you align technical execution with business strategy."}]
